items.statement: Identify the oriented standard $S^3$ with the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^4$ and fix $h(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)=x_4$. For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, there is an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy carrying $K$ to a smooth knot $K'$ for which $h|_{K'}$ has only nondegenerate critical points.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. On the unit sphere $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$ with height $h(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)=x_4$, let $c$ be a regular value and let $a$ be a smooth properly embedded arc in the upper ball $B_+=\{x_4\ge c\}$, with endpoints on $S_c=\{x_4=c\}$, such that $h|_a$ has exactly one nondegenerate interior maximum and no other critical point. For every simple smooth arc $\beta\subset S_c$ joining those endpoints, there is an embedded disk in $B_+$ with boundary $a\cup\beta$. The corresponding statement for one nondegenerate minimum in the lower ball $B_-=\{x_4\le c\}$ also holds.

items.title: A rank-one Hermitian perturbation changes signature by at most two

references.title: Ozsváth, Stipsicz, and Szabó, Grid Homology for Knots and Links
references.locator: §2.3, Exercise 2.3.2(a), printed pp. 21–22

items.statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be Hermitian forms on the same finite-dimensional complex vector space, and suppose that the linear map representing $A-B$ has rank at most one. Then $|\operatorname{sign}(A)-\operatorname{sign}(B)|\le 2$, where the signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues, with multiplicity and with zero eigenvalues omitted.

items.title: Descending-diagram crossing-change sequence

references.title: Ozsváth, Stipsicz, and Szabó, Grid Homology for Knots and Links

references.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory

items.statement: Input a valid finite planar code for one regular oriented knot diagram and a basepoint in the interior of an edge, away from every crossing and bend. Traverse the oriented code once starting at the basepoint. At each crossing, consider the first branch reached by this traversal. If that branch is under, record the crossing and exchange its over/under label; otherwise leave the crossing unchanged. Return the finite list of recorded crossing changes and the updated planar code. For a code with no crossings, return the empty list and the unchanged code. The input is the valid finite code defined for an oriented knot diagram; this procedure has no invalid-input branch.

items.title: The descending-diagram procedure terminates on admissible finite codes

references.title: Ozsváth, Stipsicz, and Szabó, Grid Homology for Knots and Links

items.statement: For every admissible finite planar code of a regular oriented knot diagram and every basepoint in the interior of an edge, the descending-diagram procedure terminates, visits each crossing record once, and returns a finite updated code and a crossing-change list with at most one entry per crossing. The updated code is admissible and its first-encounter branch at each crossing is the overpassing branch. No claim about efficient minimization of $u(K)$ is made.

items.title: A descending based knot diagram represents the unknot

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every finite rational polygonal code that records one oriented circle, finitely many transverse double points, and one overpassing branch at each double point, and every basepoint in the interior of an edge, if the first encounter at each crossing is the overpassing branch, then the represented knot is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the standard unknot.

items.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $D_+$ and $D_-$ be finite regular oriented diagrams that agree outside one crossing neighborhood and differ inside it by switching which branch is over. Let $V_+$ and $V_-$ be the Seifert matrices obtained from their oriented disk-and-band surfaces. There are corresponding integral bases in which either $V_+=V_-$ or $V_+-V_-=\pm vv^T$ for some integral column vector $v$. In particular, $\operatorname{rank}(V_+-V_-)\le1$.

Every smooth oriented knot in $S^3$ admits a finite rational polygonal code recording a one-component diagram with only finitely many transverse double points and an overpassing choice at each, together with a finite sequence of changes that switch overpassing choices and whose final diagram represents the standard unknot.

items.title: Bridge number and unknotting number of an oriented knot

references.title: Burde and Zieschang, Knots, 2nd revised and extended edition
references.locator: §2.11, printed pp. 23–24, for bridge presentations; §16.9, printed p. 339, for the standard height

references.title: Ozsváth, Stipsicz, and Szabó, Grid Homology for Knots and Links
references.locator: §2.3, printed pp. 21–25, for the unknotting number and descending diagrams

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Identify the oriented $S^3$ with the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^4$ by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism and fix the standard height $h(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)=x_4$. Its only critical points are the two poles, and each regular level is a 2-sphere. A **Morse representative** of a smooth oriented knot $K$ is a knot ambient isotopic to $K$ on which $h$ has only nondegenerate critical points. Define the **bridge number** $b(K)$ as the minimum number of local maxima of $h$ on a Morse representative of $K$. The standard unknot is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate 2-plane of $S^3$.

A **regular oriented diagram** is a projection of a smooth oriented knot with finitely many transverse double points, no other multiple points, and an over/under choice at each double point. A **crossing change** switches which branch is over at one chosen double point and leaves the projection and strand orientations unchanged. Define the **unknotting number** $u(K)$ as the minimum number of crossing changes needed to turn some regular diagram of a representative of $K$ into a diagram of the standard unknot. Both minima are taken in subsets of $\mathbb N$. The Morse-representative set is nonempty by the first well-definedness result below; under countable choice the regular-diagram existence result and the descending-diagram theorem below make the unknotting set nonempty. The bridge-number definition and the least-element argument in $\mathbb N$ require no choice; countable choice is used only to invoke the stated regular-projection supplier for $u(K)$.

items.title: Normalize a decomposing sphere relative to a bridge sphere

references.title: Seiya Negami and Kazuo Okita, The Splittability and Triviality of 3-Bridge Links
references.locator: §3, Lemma 3-3 and its proof, printed pp. 259–262; the m=2 case

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K=K_1\#K_2$ be a smooth oriented connected sum with both factors nontrivial. Let $S$ be a regular level sphere giving a bridge position: $S$ divides $S^3$ into two balls, and in each ball the knot is a finite collection of properly embedded arcs, each of which cobounds an embedded disk with an arc on $S$; the disks in each ball are pairwise disjoint. Let $P$ be a smooth decomposing sphere meeting $K$ transversely in two points and cutting it into the given two oriented factors. Put $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and let $A=P\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ be the resulting annulus, where $N(K)$ is a small closed tubular neighborhood. Assume the inclusion-induced map $\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(E)$ is injective and that there is no embedded disk in $E$, with interior disjoint from $A\cup\partial E$, whose boundary is the union of a properly embedded arc in $A$ that does not cobound a disk in $A$ with a subarc of $\partial A$ and an arc in $\partial E$. Then, after isotoping $P$ through spheres meeting $K$ twice and changing only the bridge-spanning disk systems for the fixed pair $(K,S)$, one can arrange that $P\cap S$ is exactly one simple closed curve and that the union of the upper and lower bridge-spanning disks meets $P$ in exactly two arcs, each joining one point of $P\cap K$ to a point of $P\cap S$.

items.title: Bridge number one characterizes the unknot

references.title: Jennifer Schultens, Additivity of Bridge Numbers of Knots

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice used by the bridge-number definition. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard $S^3$, $b(K)=1$ if and only if $K$ is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the fixed oriented coordinate circle used as the standard unknot.

items.title: Descending diagrams are unknotted and unknotting number is finite

references.title: Ozsváth, Stipsicz, and Szabó, Grid Homology for Knots and Links

references.locator: Definition 1 and the bridge-position discussion, printed pp. 1–2

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $D$ be an admissible finite planar code for a regular diagram of a representative of $K$, based at an interior point of an edge. The descending-diagram procedure changes at most $c(D)$ crossings, where $c(D)$ is the number of crossing records in the code, and its output diagram represents the standard unknot. Consequently the set of unknotting-sequence lengths for $K$ is a nonempty subset of $\mathbb N$, so the unknotting number $u(K)$ is finite and satisfies $u(K)\le c(D)$.

items.title: Bridge number is additive under connected sum minus one

references.title: Jennifer Schultens, Additivity of Bridge Numbers of Knots

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For any two smooth oriented knots $K$ and $J$ in $S^3$, the bridge number of their oriented connected sum satisfies
$$b(K\#J)=b(K)+b(J)-1.$$

items.title: The classical signature bounds unknotting number

items.statement:
Assume full AC. For every smooth oriented knot $K$, the classical signature $\sigma_{-1}(K)$ of the positive-push Seifert form is independent of the chosen connected spanning surface and integral basis, and it satisfies
$$|\sigma_{-1}(K)|\le 2u(K).$$
Zero eigenvalues are omitted when computing the signature of a Hermitian matrix.

items.statement: Assume full AC. For every smooth oriented knot $K$, $b(K)=1$ if and only if $K$ is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the fixed oriented coordinate circle, and the classical signature satisfies $|\sigma_{-1}(K)|\le 2u(K)$, where $u(K)$ is the minimum number of crossing changes needed to reach that circle.

items.statement: The proposed universal statement is that for every smooth oriented knot $K$ and every plane projection $D$ with finitely many transverse double points, no other multiple points, and a chosen overpassing branch at each double point, the number $c(D)$ of double points equals the unknotting number $u(K)$.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $T$ be the standard right-handed trefoil represented by the closure of the two-strand braid with three positive crossings. In its standard oriented three-crossing projection, label the under-arcs $a,b,c$ so that the crossing triples $(o,t,s)$ of over-arc, target under-arc and source under-arc are $(b,c,a)$, $(c,a,b)$ and $(a,b,c)$, where source and target are determined by the positive in-plane normal to the oriented over-strand. Define bridge number as the minimum number of local maxima over Morse representatives in the fixed standard height on $S^3$, and unknotting number as the minimum number of crossing changes needed to turn a regular diagram of a representative into the fixed standard unknot diagram. Then $b(T)=2$ and $u(T)=1$.
